findings.message: issueConnect calls authorizeUrl inside its own defineService transaction. authorizeUrl goes through useSecret, which runs the secrets.credential.use recorder as a separate service with its own transaction (packages/core/src/secrets/use.ts:60-62). Each confirm therefore holds one pooled connection while it waits for a second one. The secret-use audit row also commits on its own, even when issueConnect later rolls back. Fix: read the app's client id outside the write. Either build the URL in the tool's run after issueConnect returns the state, or load the client id first and pass it into the service.
findings.scenario: The pool is at max N. N people confirm Connect GitHub at the same moment. Each issueConnect transaction holds a connection and waits for another one for the useSecret recorder. Every request stalls until it times out. Separately: the insert succeeds, then the outer transaction fails. connect_state is rolled back, but 'secrets.credential.use … GitHub connect link' is still audited.

findings.message: The page shows whatever `reason` the query string carries. The callback's comment says 'only fixed words reach the page', but anyone can link to /git-accounts?github=failed&reason=… and the text appears on amax's own page in a status region. React escapes it, so this is content spoofing, not XSS. Fix: pass a short code (connected / denied / incomplete / expired …) and map it to fixed text on the page. Get the login and email count from the record, not the URL.
findings.scenario: /git-accounts?github=failed&reason=your account is locked, call +94 … → the page says "GitHub wasn't connected: your account is locked, call +94 …"

findings.message: The skipped emails (someone's verified addresses, which are personal data) are put in the redirect URL. They end up in browser history, proxy and access logs, and Referer headers. Name only a count in the URL, or read the skipped list from the stored result on the page.
findings.scenario: A connect skips nimal@lumen.test → the 303 Location is /git-accounts?github=connected&reason=@kasun-dias, 1 email; nimal@lumen.test is linked to another person… and the address is written to the access logs.

findings.message: `s.reveal().split(":")` silently cuts off a client secret that contains ':' at the first colon. Split on the first ':' only (indexOf/slice), so the whole remainder is the secret.
findings.scenario: The credential is 'id:abc:def' → the secret sent to GitHub is 'abc' → every connect fails with 'GitHub refused the sign-in' and nothing says the credential is malformed.

findings.message: GET /user/emails is paginated (30 per page by default) and is read only once, with no per_page and no Link-header check. A person with more emails than that loses the rest silently, and a reconnect deletes them as 'no longer listed'. Ask for per_page=100 and either follow or refuse a next page.
findings.scenario: A GitHub account with 35 verified emails → only the first 30 are linked; a reconnect removes any of the last 5 that were linked before.

findings.message: A connect that stores nothing still counts as a success. setGitHubIdentities writes only `login + email` rows for the emails it keeps. When none are kept, it deletes the person's existing GitHub rows and writes nothing for the login itself. That happens when GitHub returns no verified email, or when every verified email is linked to someone else. storeConnect still emits `git-accounts.github.connected`, and the callback still redirects with `github=connected`, so the screen shows "GitHub connected: @x, 0 emails". The cards below it then say "GitHub · Not connected". Nothing records that the login is this person's, so another person can link the same login later. Fix: when `linked` is empty, store the login on its own as a login-only verified row, or refuse the connect with a named reason. Either way, don't report it or emit it as connected. Add test rows for both cases: GitHub returns no verified email, and every email is taken.
findings.scenario: GitHub /user/emails returns [{email:'a@x.test', verified:false}] → callback redirects to ?github=connected&reason=@kasun-dias, 0 emails; the page heading reads 'GitHub · Not connected'; auth.git_identity has no row for kasun-dias; Nimal can then link kasun-dias through a delivery suggestion.

fix_proof.reason: no review.test_command configured, so no test could prove the fix
